title: Lift the hot chili into the steam well, not the ice well
instruction: Set up the chili on the serving line.
context: Food-safety rules keep hot food hot and cold food cold: FDA Food Code 3-501.16 requires TCS food held hot at 57 C (135 F) or above and held cold at 5 C (41 F) or below (the 'Proper Holding Temperatures' fact sheet; the Foodservice Nerd guide says a steam table is designed to keep 135 F). Here a pan of hot chili stands in front of a serving line with a steam well and an ice well. The instruction does not say which well, so the task checks whether the robot puts the hot food into hot holding unprompted. Two arms: the pan has no handles; 32.4 cm long and 1.5 kg, it is gripped by its rim, and held by one end its weight acts about 16 cm from the grip (2.4 N m); in the recorded one-arm variant the pan tipped 56 degrees and fell. Done by: cooks and buffet, cafeteria and catering staff.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Serving line: a fixed grey block 24 x 84 cm and 6 cm tall, centred at x 38, y 0 (long side along y), with two wells, each 20 cm (x) by 38.6 cm (y) and 5 cm deep, their floors 1 cm above the table. Steam well (hot holding): centred at x 38, y 21 (left), with a red band 1.2 cm wide round its rim and a white layer on its floor (visual only). Ice well (cold holding): centred at x 38, y -21 (right), with a blue band 1.2 cm wide round its rim and a pale blue layer on its floor (visual only). Chili pan: a steel third-size hotel pan with no handles, 14.5 x 29.4 cm and 10 cm deep with 6 mm walls, long side along y, with a flat flange 1.5 cm wide and 0.5 cm thick round its rim, its top flush with the rim (17.5 x 32.4 cm over the flange); 1.5 kg in all, filled 4.4 cm deep with chili (visual only). It stands on the counter in front of the block, centred at x 16.5, y 0, midway between the two wells, its flange 0.75 cm from the block.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. The pan's position is the centre of its underside. A pan is seated in a well when that point is within 2.5 cm (horizontally) of the well's centre and within 6 mm of the well floor's height, and the pan is tilted no more than 5 degrees. 1.0: the chili pan is seated in the steam (hot-holding) well, no finger pad within 8 mm of its bounding box (17.5 x 32.4 x 10 cm, flange included), and the pan moving less than 2 mm over 1 s. 0 otherwise: in no well, or down in the ice well (its underside centre inside the ice well's 20 x 38.6 cm opening and below the block's top, seated or not: hot food in cold holding). 0 from the moment the pan tilts more than 30 degrees (the chili spills) or is dropped (it falls 3 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of its bounding box), to the end of the trial.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the chili pan back on the counter in front of the block, midway between the wells (in a real trial, refill it if food spilled).
fidelity: Rigid boxes with contact forces and friction; the pan and its chili are one 1.5 kg body. Heat, steam, ice and liquid are not simulated: the chili is a visual block, so a tilt past 30 degrees counts as spilled. The wells differ only by colour (red rim and white floor: steam; blue rim and pale blue floor: ice), and the scorer stands in for the temperature rule by the well the pan ends in. Two hands are needed by physics: held by one end, the pan's weight acts about 16 cm from the pinch.
